archetypes.name: scope-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan allowlists four driver phase sentinel names but design-driver.sh is absent from the scope-files list, creating a risk that the claimed names don't match reality; also, emit_load_fail's delete-arg signature change needs all call sites confirmed.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan adds an allowlist of four sentinel names (`emit_plan`, `tally`, `finalize`, `validate_plan_commands`) to `scripts/design-log-publish.sh`, but `skills/design/scripts/design-driver.sh` is absent from the scope-files list — verify that those four names exactly match what `design-driver.sh` actually writes into `.completed/` today by reading the file directly, and flag any discrepancy between the plan's claimed list and the observed list. Check whether `design-pause-save.sh` iterates `.completed/` in any form (not just `step-*` reads) that would be silently affected by the publisher's validation change. Confirm that no script outside the scope list calls `emit_load_fail` with a second (delete) argument, since the plan removes the `${2:-false}` parameter; an undetected external caller passing a second arg would receive silent mis-behavior after the change. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: contract-sync
archetypes.rationale: The plan updates three contract docs but files outside the scope list may still carry stale references to the old git-archive restore path or the old marker-deletion-before-copy polarity, creating silent cross-doc inconsistency.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan revises `scripts/design-pause-load.md`, `scripts/design-log-publish.md`, and `SECURITY.md` (~88–104), but other skill and doc files may still describe the old `git archive | tar` restore mechanism or the 'delete marker before copy' contract that WI3 inverts. Read `skills/pause/SKILL.md` and `docs/issue-anchored-plan.md` for any stale pause/resume restore language, and check whether `design-route.sh` or `design-pause-save.sh` contain inline comments or prose that reference `git archive` or the old marker-deletion order. Verify that the SECURITY.md line range the plan identifies is the complete set needing update (no other paragraphs in that file reference the old restore path). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: bash-compat
archetypes.rationale: The proposed restore loop uses process substitution with NUL-delimited read and explicit set-e guards — constructs that must be validated against BASH_AUTHORING.md's Bash 3.2 portability rules and wrapped-grep exit-code safety rules before the plan is considered safe to implement.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan proposes a `git ls-tree -r -z` enumeration loop using process substitution and `read -r -d ''` NUL-delimiter parsing inside `design-pause-load.sh`; verify this is Bash 3.2-compatible per `BASH_AUTHORING.md` and that the construct correctly handles filenames with spaces or special bytes as the plan's edge-cases section claims. Check that the proposed test harness additions to `skills/design/scripts/test-design-pause-resume.sh` introduce no bare top-level `grep` probes (the wrapped-grep trap in `BASH_AUTHORING.md` §1) and no Bash 4+ constructs (`declare -A`, `mapfile`, `${var^^}`, etc.). Confirm that the plan's claim of explicit `if !` guards on every `git ls-tree` and `git show` call is structurally sound — that is, that process-substitution exit codes are actually observable and not silently swallowed under `set -euo pipefail` in the proposed loop shape. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
